verdicts.reason: A separates the can from its circle and puts the CTA and both badges on top of the bare circle at the right edge. The CTA there is tiny, the same weight as the badges, and the pills look jammed together. GLACIER also sits below the headline. B also splits the backdrop circle from the can, leaving an empty circle on the left and the can on the right, so the main image loses its meaning, and its CTA is still badge-sized. But the text block, buttons and badges read in a clean left-aligned stack with no collisions.

A has the same flaws as pair 1's B: an empty circle detached from the can, the brand name below the headline, and a CTA no bigger than the badges. But it is tidy and readable. B is unusable: the headline and GLACIER sit on top of the circle, the product can has shrunk to a speck next to a tiny CTA in the bottom-right corner, 'Back by demand' can barely be read, and 'Summer only' floats on its own, leaving a large dead area.
